problem.title: Deadlock via Non-Hierarchical Multi-Lock Acquisition (AB vs. BA Locking)
problem.prompt: E-commerce fund transfer service acquiring mutexes on Account A and Account B concurrently across two competing transactions.
requirements: Operational Invariant: "Multi-resource locks must strictly follow a globally deterministic acquisition hierarchy to prevent cycle formation."

stages.learnerPrompt: What catastrophic failure physics occur when capacity limits or downstream dependencies degrade under peak load?

referenceMaterial.summary: Failure physics analysis: Burst → Pool Saturated → Queue Bloat (10k) → STW GC → 💥 504 Timeouts.
failureModes: Cascading Failure: Thread 1 locks Account A then attempts to lock Account B; Thread 2 locks Account B then attempts to lock Account A. Under concurrent transfer , both threads block indefinitely, causing complete worker pool deadlock.
Breakdown Chain: Burst → Pool Saturated → Queue Bloat (10k) → STW GC → 💥 504 Timeouts
Shedding Failure: Without fast rejection at the boundary, queued dead work triggers multi-second GC pauses, CPU thrashing, and cascading 504 Gateway Timeouts.

stages.learnerPrompt: How does the system enforce physical resource boundaries under sudden downstream latency brownouts?

referenceMaterial.summary: Senior Staff SRE Interview challenge and architectural invariant verification.
tradeOffs: Architectural Invariant: "Multi-resource locks must strictly follow a globally deterministic acquisition hierarchy to prevent cycle formation."
Physical Resource Boundary: Dynamic admission control ensures worker threads never buffer dead requests during downstream brownouts.
approachSteps: 1. Track real-time latency gradients and inflight concurrency.
2. Reject excess traffic at the ingress boundary within <0.1ms.
3. Monitor P99 latency and verify autonomous recovery when downstream pressure subsides.
